objective: Determine whether a standalone program reproduces the closed qualification's LeakSanitizer shutdown failure, and whether separately authorized unrestricted execution permits leak scanning.
native_control_side_effects: Temporary process allocations and two joined threads only; stdout diagnostics. No filesystem or network operations. The leak mode intentionally leaves one 4096-byte allocation until process exit.
environment_hypothesis: Both cleanup modes fail with LeakSanitizer's fatal scanning error inside the sandbox, but exit zero outside it; outside execution of the deliberate leak exits 66 with a leak report instead of a scanning error.
execution_authority: The unrestricted phase must be invoked through exec_command with require_escalated, after the exact standalone source, binary and sandbox results are reviewable. Do not infer that permission from elapsed time.
failure_policy: Preserve every stdout, stderr and code. Stop on any native exit other than 0 or 66. A completed diagnostic is not a successful library qualification. Do not rerun, extend or pool this six-execution protocol.
limits: The test does not modify or resume the failed library qualification.
The standard library remains precompiled; no new production proof or memory-safety coverage claim.
Successful standalone controls do not establish that repository tests pass under the same configuration.
The observed context comparison can identify a sandbox-associated scanning restriction without proving which kernel permission caused it.
